Amrita Kumari Dixit @ Amrita Kindo vs Central Bureau Of
Investigation .... ... on 19 October, 2023

Author: Sashikanta Mishra
Bench: Sashikanta Mishra
 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Ablapl No. 11539 of 2023
 Amrita Kumari Dixit @ Amrita Kindo ....

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Petitioner
 Mr. B.N. Mohanty, Advocate
 -versus-
 Central Bureau of Investigation .... Opposite Party
 Mr. Sarthak Nayak, Standing Counsel for Cbi
 Coram:
 Justice Sashikanta Mishra
 Order
Order No. 19.10.2023
02. 1.
This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

2. The Petitioner is apprehending arrest in connection with Khorda DSPE, CBI, ACB, Bhubaneswar Case No. RC 08(A)/2023-BBS for the alleged commission of offence under Sections 120- B/420/409/468/471 of IPC read with Sections 13(2) and 13(1)(d) of Prevention of Corruption Act,
1988, Section 13(1)(a) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

3. The prosecution case is that the Petitioner conspired with one Deepak Kindo, who is her husband,
and facilitated illegal transfer of funds by falsifying the accounts.
The funds so diverted had actually been obtained as loans by the Principal concern, namely, M/s. Sambandh Finserve Private Limited (SFPL) of which Deepak Kindo is the Managing Director.

After obtaining loans from different financial entities including SIDBI, Deepak Kindo diverted and siphoned the funds to different entities/individuals through falsification of records and statements.
Some of the funds were found to have been transferred to the account of the present Petitioner.
On the basis of a complaint lodged by the Officer of SIDBI, the aforementioned case has been registered by the CBI.

4. Heard Mr. B.N. Mohanty, learned counsel for the Petitioner and Mr. Sarthak Nayak, learned Standing Counsel for the Opposite Party-CBI.
5.
It is submitted by Mr. Mohanty, learned counsel that the Petitioner has no role whatsoever to play in the alleged falsification of records and diversion of funds.

She has been entangled in the case only Amrita Kumari Dixit @ Amrita Kindo vs Central Bureau Of Investigation .... ... on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43138312/
1 to harass her as she was released on bail by this Court in a connected case.

entities.text: Amrita Kumari Dixit @ Amrita Kindo vs Central Bureau Of Investigation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that even otherwise, the Petitioner is a lady having several physical ailments and her husband is in jail custody.
As a result, she is facing a lot of hardships in maintaining herself and her only minor daughter.

6. Mr. Sarthak Nayak, learned counsel on the other hand, has opposed the prayer for bail by submitting that there are adequate materials to prima facie show the involvement of the present Petitioner in the alleged occurrence.
The fact that she was granted bail in a connected case has no bearing on the present case, which has been registered on a separate though similar cause of action.
7. I have considered the rival submissions and the materials on record.

8. So far as the present Petitioner is concerned, the allegation is that she was party to the diversion of the funds by M/s. SFPL obtained as loans from different financial institutions, which are said to be eight (08) in number.
It is alleged that a total sum of Rs.141.88 Crores is involved in the process.
Further the Petitioner is the Managing Director of a firm called Diya Dairy and Agro Processor Private Limited (DDAPL), which is stated to be a sister concern of M/s. SFPL, owned by her husband.

entities.text: Diya Dairy and Agro Processor Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
There is evidence to show transfer of funds to the account of the said company, namely DDAPL.
9.
It is true that the Petitioner has been granted bail in a connected case as per the order passed in BLAPL No.2818 of 2022 by imposing stringent conditions.
The conditions so imposed have not been violated.

It is trite law that economic offences need to be viewed seriously and, therefore, ordinarily this Court would be slow to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner, particularly, in view of the prima facie evidence of her involvement in the occurrence.

Nevertheless, this Court finds that the Petitioner is a lady and appears to be suffering from several ailments as evident from the copies of the medical documents enclosed to the bail application under Annexure-4.
Her minor daughter aged about 12 years is also suffering from some gynaecological ailments.
10. There is no dispute that the husband of the Petitioner is in custody and there is no other male member available in the family.
As already stated, the Petitioner has not violated the conditions imposed by this Court while granting her bail in the connected case.
11. Thus, this Court is inclined to take a lenient view purely on humanitarian consideration.

While not being inclined to grant anticipatory bail, the ABLAPL is disposed of granting liberty to the Petitioner to surrender before the Court below within two weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order and to move for bail.

In such event, she shall be released on bail on such terms and conditions as the Court below may deem fit and proper to impose including the condition that she shall fully cooperate with the investigation as required by the Investigating Officer.
(Sashikanta Mishra) Judge S. Behera
